traceability.evidence:
- Story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md defines requirements for ESLint configuration presets, ESLint v9 flat config support, customizable paths, rule options, project integration, and configuration validation.
- Core presets (REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS, REQ-FLAT-CONFIG): - In src/index.ts, TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES defines severities for all traceability rules. - createTraceabilityFlatConfig returns a flat-config object with a rules map based on TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES and is annotated with this story and REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS. - configs.recommended and configs.strict are arrays of config objects [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], matching ESLint v9 flat config expectations and intended to be spread into consumer configs after a plugins object. - tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts (tagged with @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md and @req REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS, REQ-FLAT-CONFIG, REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION) uses ESLint FlatESLint with overrideConfig as a flat-config array [baseConfig, ...configs.recommended] and [baseConfig, ...configs.strict] and verifies that linting a simple function reports the traceability/require-story-annotation rule. This confirms the presets work as documented in an ESLint v9 flat-config environment.
- ESLint v9 flat config best practices (Quality Standards, REQ-FLAT-CONFIG): - eslint.config.js is itself an ESLint v9 flat config (module.exports = [ ... ]) and is annotated with this story and REQ-FLAT-CONFIG. It uses js.configs.recommended from @eslint/js, file-based overrides for TS, JS, config files, and tests, plus ignores, aligning with flat-config best practices. - The presets in src/index.ts are pure rule-severity maps and do not attempt legacy eslintrc style extends, which is correct for ESLint v9.
- Rule options and configuration validation (REQ-RULE-OPTIONS, REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION, Error Handling AC): - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts declares a meta.schema with properties storyDirectories (array of strings), allowAbsolutePaths (boolean), and requireStoryExtension (boolean), and sets additionalProperties to false to reject unknown options. - tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts asserts that this schema exposes the expected properties and that additionalProperties is false, covering REQ-RULE-OPTIONS and REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION. - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts meta.schema exposes options scope (array of strings from DEFAULT_SCOPE) and exportPriority (string from EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES) with additionalProperties false. - tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts asserts that schema.properties includes scope and exportPriority and that additionalProperties is false, further confirming REQ-RULE-OPTIONS. - src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts meta.schema defines a branchTypes array option with uniqueItems true and additionalProperties false. - src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts implements validateBranchTypes, which checks provided branchTypes against DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES and, if invalid, returns a listener that reports clear, per-value error messages (for example: Value X should be equal to one of the allowed values: IfStatement, SwitchCase, TryStatement, …). - tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts verifies this behavior by ensuring the listener reports for each invalid type with messages containing the allowed values list. - tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts includes a case named [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE] invalid branchTypes option should error schema, passing branchTypes with an unknown type and asserting that an error message matching /should be equal to one of the allowed values/ is produced. - Combined schema-based validation (additionalProperties false) and explicit runtime validation for branchTypes provide graceful handling of invalid configuration options, satisfying the story’s Error Handling and REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION requirements even though the acceptance checkbox remains unchecked in the markdown.
- Customizable story paths and locations (REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS): - In src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts, defaultStoryDirs is set to ['docs/stories', 'stories'], and the create function reads options.storyDirectories, options.allowAbsolutePaths, and options.requireStoryExtension to drive behavior. - The rule uses utility functions like normalizeStoryPath, performSecurityValidations, and handleProjectBoundaryForExistence, along with configuration, to check story paths, enforce boundaries, and validate extensions. - tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts (per Jest verbose output) includes multiple tests tagged [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS], such as: - honors custom storyDirectories using docs/stories, - allowAbsolutePaths accepts existing absolute .story.md inside project, - accepts .story.md story path when requireStoryExtension is false, - and additional tests under Valid Story Reference Rule Configuration and Boundaries verifying that storyDirectories are used while enforcing project boundaries. - This proves that story file locations and patterns are configurable via rule options, satisfying REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS.
- Project integration (REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION, Integration AC): - The presets in src/index.ts only define rule severities and assume the consumer registers the plugin beforehand, minimizing conflicts with existing ESLint setups. - flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts shows realistic use where a baseConfig registers the plugin under plugins.traceability and an empty rules object, then spreads ...configs.recommended or ...configs.strict into the flat-config array. Linting a simple JS function yields expected traceability rule messages, confirming integration. - README.md provides a concise example eslint.config.js that combines @eslint/js recommended config with the plugin’s recommended preset, showing how to integrate this plugin into an existing ESLint configuration. - user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md contains extensive examples for JavaScript-only, TypeScript-only, mixed JS/TS, monorepo/workspaces, Node config files, and test files, all integrating the plugin by registering traceability under plugins and then spreading traceability.configs.recommended or strict. This wide coverage satisfies REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION and the Integration acceptance criterion.
- User experience and documentation (User Experience AC, Documentation AC): - README.md references ESLint v9, shows a minimal working eslint.config.js using this plugin’s recommended preset, lists available rules, and links to detailed user docs (ESLint 9 Setup Guide, API Reference, Examples, Migration Guide). - user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md documents: - Flat-config format, ESM vs CommonJS, and key changes from eslintrc. - Common configuration patterns with complete copy-pasteable examples for JS, TS, mixed projects, tests, monorepos, and Node config files, including how to register the traceability plugin and apply its presets. - Common issues and solutions and a Troubleshooting ESLint Configuration section that covers frequent misconfigurations and their remedies. - These materials provide clear setup guidance, examples for common project types, and troubleshooting, meeting the User Experience and Documentation acceptance criteria.
- Test evidence: - npm test -- --verbose completed successfully with 35 passed test suites and 264 passed tests. - Among them: - tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts (Story 002.0) passed, confirming flat-config preset behavior. - tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts (Story 002.0) passed, confirming rule option schemas and validation. - tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts (Story 002.0) passed, confirming rule option schema for require-story-annotation. - Additional rule and helper tests validate customizable paths and invalid configuration handling (valid-story-reference, require-branch-annotation, branch-annotation-helpers), giving strong automated evidence that the config system behaves as specified.
traceability.notes:
Based on the inspected implementation, tests, and user documentation, all functional and documentation-related requirements for story 002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG are satisfied.
The plugin exposes recommended and strict presets as ESLint v9 flat-config arrays intended to be spread after a plugins registration object. Integration tests using FlatESLint verify these presets correctly enable the plugin’s rules. Rule-specific configuration options are declared via JSON schemas with additionalProperties set to false, and both schema-based and runtime checks produce clear errors when options are invalid, covering configuration validation and error handling. Customization of story file locations and paths is implemented through valid-story-reference rule options and extensively tested, including security and project-boundary behavior.
Project integration is demonstrated in tests (FlatESLint overrideConfig usage) and in multiple documentation examples spanning JS, TS, mixed projects, and monorepos. README.md and the ESLint 9 Setup Guide provide clear, concrete configuration and troubleshooting guidance for end users. Although the Error Handling checkbox remains unchecked in the story markdown, the actual code and tests show graceful handling of invalid configuration options. Therefore, this story is considered fully implemented and passes.
